title: Tidal Dwarf Galaxies as a Test of History-Dependent Inertia: How a Long-Memory Kernel Can Leave Young Dwarfs Near-Newtonian
description: Tidal dwarf galaxies (TDGs) -- condensations formed from tidal debris pulled from a progenitor disc during a galaxy interaction -- are the classic sign-flip test between dark matter and modified dynamics: in LCDM they are born devoid of non-baryonic dark matter and should be Newtonian (Mdyn/Mbar ~ 1), while in INSTANTANEOUS modified dynamics (modified gravity AQUAL/QUMOND, or short-memory modified inertia) they sit deep in the low-acceleration regime (current g_bar/a0 = 0.015-0.073; Lelli et al. 2015) and should show a large boost (nu ~ 6, Mdyn/Mbar ~ 4-8). The best HI kinematics (Lelli et al. 2015, six TDGs around NGC 5291 and NGC 7252 plus VCC 2062) instead give Mdyn/Mbar = 0.9-1.5: near-Newtonian. Instantaneous modified dynamics over-predicts the rotation velocities even with the external-field effect, at roughly 2-3 sigma per NGC 5291 object (the lower framework a0 = 9.355e-11 vs the standard 1.2e-10 helps by only ~6%). This paper reads the same data through the de Sitter-Unruh MODIFIED-INERTIA framework, using its OWN interpolation nu(y) = sqrt(1+1/y), its own footings (canonical a0 = 9.355e-11 = cH_Lambda/Z / alt 1.1305e-10, both carried), and its COMMITTED memory kernel tau_mem = 2Z/H_Lambda = 203 Gyr (the same kernel used in the relational sigma-spread and SHLEM analyses). Because TDG ages (~0.36 Gyr) are minute compared with tau_mem, the debris gas has NOT relaxed to its current deep-regime inertia; its effective inertia is dominated by the ~10-13 Gyr it spent at higher acceleration in the progenitor disc. Averaging the RESPONSE nu the way the framework's own sigma-spread analysis does (a Jensen gap over the convex nu, with residence-time weight w ~ 0.36/13.8 ~ 2.6% for the recent low-acceleration epoch, since the committed kernel is power-law/non-saturating), a plausible outer-disc history (y_hist ~ 0.5-2) gives nu_eff ~ 1.4-1.9, i.e. Mdyn/Mbar ~ 1.4-1.9. This RESOLVES the gross factor-~4 instantaneous over-prediction (nu ~ 6 -> ~1.5) but lands at the HIGH EDGE of, and mildly above, the observed range (over-predicting the older, lower-mass NGC 7252/VCC by a few tenths, within their +/-0.6 errors) -- a consistency, not a bullseye. The freeze is defended by the committed formalism, not asserted: the field-theory closure carries a single scale a0 and rejects any orbital-time (dynamical) relaxation corner as a new scale absent from the action, so the 203-Gyr memory is orbit-independent and the debris does not re-equilibrate on a galaxy dynamical time. HONEST SCOPE, stated prominently BOTH WAYS: (GAIN) TDGs become a candidate HISTORY-DEPENDENCE discriminator -- instantaneous modified dynamics is disfavored at ~2-3 sigma while long-memory modified inertia and LCDM both survive; a new member of the framework's history-dependence family (with the sigma-spread and SHLEM), and the first with data at least compatible with the memory-kernel direction. (COST, up front) under the long-memory reading the framework predicts the SAME near-Newtonian TDGs as LCDM, so the classic sign-flip discriminator against dark matter DISSOLVES for this framework -- this paper must NOT be read as 'TDGs show no dark matter' or as confirmation of the framework. (CAVEAT 1) Lelli's own non-equilibrium escape (TDG orbital times >> ages -> discs may be unsettled -> Vcirc underestimates the potential) ALSO rescues instantaneous MOND, so 'long-memory MI' and 'instantaneous MOND + non-equilibrium' are degenerate on current data. (CAVEAT 2) the nu_eff mapping is kernel-hostage: the outer-disc history y_hist is assumed (least-bound-gas prior skews it low, nu_eff high), and the averaging rule is unpinned (response-averaging gives 1.4-1.9, the generic acceleration-averaging shortcut gives a lower, more favorable 1.2-1.7 -- a ~20-30% swing). (CAVEAT 3, self-correction on the record) the first pass of this analysis wrongly reported a ~2-3 sigma tension AGAINST the framework by applying the instantaneous (standard-lens) prediction to a theory that commits to a 203-Gyr kernel; that adverse verdict is retracted and re-scoped to instantaneous modified gravity and short-memory inertia. HONEST WARNING on the forecast: the touted age-vs-discrepancy gradient (older TDGs -> more boost) runs the WRONG way in the present sample (older NGC 7252 has LOWER Mdyn/Mbar than younger NGC 5291), within errors but not supporting evidence. The values of a0, Z, and the map from the 203-Gyr history average to nu_eff remain posited or estimated, not derived. CREDIT: the TDG-MOND test and the data are Gentile et al. 2007 (A&A 472 L25, who found consistency with higher assumed velocities + EFE), Bournaud et al. 2007, and Lelli et al. 2015 (A&A 584 A113); nonlocal/history-dependent modified inertia is Milgrom 1994 (Ann. Phys. 229, 384); the interpolation kernel is Milgrom 1999 (PLA 253:273); the TDG non-equilibrium caution is Lelli 2015 / Kroupa. Novelty coverage caveat: a search found no prior long-memory-MI reading of the TDG data; 'no duplicate found' is not 'none exists'. Every load-bearing number is produced by the committed, exit-0 script tdg_test.py.
notes: Referee-graded writeup (draft -> 3-reviewer adversarial panel [physics(nu_eff crux)/honesty+privacy/citation] -> revise). The physics panel forced two corrections: (1) the central claim was DOWNGRADED from a firm prediction to a plausibility estimate + hypothesis + forecast -- the 203-Gyr kernel FIRMLY forbids the deep-regime boost for 0.36-Gyr debris (qualitative), but the quantitative Mdyn/Mbar landing is kernel-hostage; (2) the nu_eff estimate was re-computed with the FRAMEWORK'S OWN averaging prescription (response-averaging / Jensen gap over convex nu, per the sigma-spread paper) giving ~1.4-1.9 at the HIGH EDGE of the data, replacing the draft's more-favorable generic y-averaging (~1.2-1.7). The freeze is defended via the closure single-scale/orbital-corner-rejection result; the in-sample age-gradient wrong-sign is flagged. Framework flavor enforced throughout: canonical a0 = 9.36e-11 + alt footing, nu(y)=sqrt(1+1/y), the 203-Gyr MI kernel -- the standard a0 = 1.2e-10 appears ONLY as Lelli's rival baseline. Privacy audit: zero personal info beyond the author byline.
